input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper's statistics dict is cleared and then shared by every call, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated function write into one dict and reset each other's statistics.
- rationale: Trigger: two coroutines await the same decorated function at the same time. Mechanism: each call runs stats.clear() on the shared wrapper dict and then assigns that dict to its copy's _local.statistics, so attempt_number and start_time from one call are overwritten by the other. Impact: statistics read from the wrapper (or from retry_state) are silently wrong. The original code gave each call its own copy.statistics dict, which avoided this.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: one statistics dict is reused across calls, so concurrent awaits run stats.clear() and overwrite each other's start_time and attempt_number. It also notes the original per-call dict, which is the root cause the label gives.
